text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD alert `PD#98765` - gpu-node-west2a: cuda::alloc failed (OOM) x 18 in last 5m. Auto-page triggered. <https://pagerduty.com/incident/PD#98765>

alex_oncall: saw the page, I'm acking now :raising_hand:

alex_oncall: logs show repeated `cudaMalloc` failures on gpu-node-12, nvml reports 99% mem

maya_infra: thanks, checking node metrics and kswap/dmesg

sre-lead: any customer-facing errors? support-john, FYI

support-john: one customer (acct: acme-corp) reported 503s starting ~10:02 UTC. I've opened a ticket.

maya_infra: `dmesg` shows repeated mmap ENOMEM and kernel reclaim kicks. kvcache eviction spiked ~10:00

alex_oncall: temporarily rerouting new allocation traffic away from node-12 via pool drain

incident-bot: Auto-scale policy triggered +1 GPU pool in west2 region (requested), ETA ~3m

sre-lead: good. Alex, can you attempt a graceful restart of the inference worker on node-12 once drain completes?

alex_oncall: starting graceful shutdown on node-12 processes now, will wait for in-flight to finish

maya_infra: there's also high memory fragmentation across the pool — thinking a VM-level reclaim won't clear fragmentation. Suspect kv-cache fragmentation + large batch requests.

sre-lead: mitigation plan: 1) drain node-12 (in progress) 2) spin up replacement instances (in progress) 3) scale down aggressive batch sizes for live service (config push) 4) follow-up postmortem if recurrent

alex_oncall: pushed temp config to reduce max_batch_tokens=512 -> 256 for heavy customers

support-john: letting acme-corp know we routed their traffic and we're mitigating. ETA message -> "intermittent 503s, routing and scaling underway"

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD#98765 acknowledged by alex_oncall

maya_infra: node-12 worker stopped, instance marked draining. New instance spun (gpu-node-19) and joined pool.

alex_oncall: observed successful allocations on new node-19. memory usage stable.

sre-lead: handing off to infra for follow-up and deep dive. Maya, please own the postmortem and heap/fragmentation analysis. Alex keep monitoring for 15m then stand down.

maya_infra: will investigate kv eviction patterns and any batch job anomalies. grabbing kernel coredumps and nvprof traces.

support-john: updated acme-corp: "we routed your traffic and provisioned capacity, service should be stable; we'll follow up with root cause"

alex_oncall: monitoring metrics — no further OOMs in the pool for 12m. marking as resolved in Slack if stable for 20m :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: PD#98765 resolved by alex_oncall

sre-lead: thanks team. Quick notes: avoid large concurrent batches during next autoscale window; maya please add suggested throttles to runbook.

maya_infra: will add to runbook + create an alert for kvcache eviction rate > 500/min

support-john: closing customer ticket once maya confirms postmortem draft

alex_oncall: standing down, will reopen if anything flares. :v:
